summary: Backend testing complete for Onyx Electronics. 31 pytest tests PASSED, 1 skipped (test_emi_below_threshold — no seed product priced under $200 EMI threshold; not a bug). Covered: auth (register/login/me/RBAC), products (list/get/categories/filter), EMI (config/calculate/update-config w/ role guards), cart flow (add/get/remove), orders (full & EMI with schedule generation and stock decrement), EMI installment payment (+ duplicate rejection), admin endpoints (stats/users/orders/emis/approve/reject) with 403 checks for customer and inventory_manager, inventory endpoints (stats/low-stock/restock) with 403 for customer. Verified no Mongo `_id` leaks in any response payload via recursive traversal. All endpoints returned expected status codes and data structures.

minor.issue: No seeded product is priced below the default EMI threshold ($200) — makes 'below threshold' EMI rejection path uncoverable by realistic customer flow. Cheapest product is Sony WH-1000XM5 at $399. Consider adding an accessory (<$200) or lowering threshold in demo config.

Test-only observation: EMI order is created with status 'confirmed' AND stock is decremented BEFORE admin approval. If EMI approval is meant to gate fulfillment, stock/confirmation should only occur after admin approves (currently 'pending' approval_status has no effect on order lifecycle).
Endpoint allows customer to mark EMI installments paid even when emi.approval_status is still 'pending' or 'rejected'. Should likely require approved status.
Uses $inc so negative quantity would silently reduce stock. Add validation quantity > 0 in RestockIn model.

action_items: (Optional) Add a <$200 accessory product to seed data so the EMI-threshold rejection path is exercised end-to-end.
(Business decision) Consider gating stock decrement and order confirmation on EMI approval, and reject pay-emi calls when approval_status != 'approved'.
Add positive-quantity validation on RestockIn (currently allows negative $inc).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 525 lines — still within recommended threshold but growing; splitting into routers (auth/products/orders/admin/inventory) will improve maintainability as features are added.
All Mongo reads correctly project out `_id` (verified). Good.
JWT_SECRET falls back to a hard-coded default when env var missing — acceptable for demo but flag for production.
get_current_user projects out password on user fetch — good.
No pagination on /api/admin/orders and /api/admin/users (currently 500 doc cap). Acceptable for demo; add pagination before scale.
seed_data_creation: Tests create ephemeral TEST_-prefixed user accounts on each run (via /auth/register). No cleanup performed (no admin delete-user endpoint exposed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py runs against external URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. Uses pytest-xdist LoadScopeScheduling (classes to same worker) — do NOT introduce cross-class stock arithmetic assertions (they will race). Seeded accounts: admin@onyx.com/admin123, inventory@onyx.com/inventory123, customer@onyx.com/customer123. All endpoints under /api prefix.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. Two initial test failures during authoring were test-data/race issues on my side, not backend defects: (1) test assumed a <$200 product existed in seed data; (2) restock assertion race with parallel order tests decrementing stock. Both fixed in the test file.
